# CardDemo parity oracle audit

This audit records what the COBOL oracle does, so that the Rust and web replacement can be written and tested against it. Each row is one decision of a carried program, copybook, JCL step or fixture, cited to the physical lines it comes from. Defect-like behaviour is recorded as the COBOL performs it; anomalous fixtures are read as their bytes say. Rows whose result cannot be pinned from the repository and IBM documentation name a `halt` escalation instead of a guess.

Author: `blitzy-audit-author`. Reviewer of every row: `blitzy-cobol-reviewer`. Escalations raised here are listed in the last section and carried into `docs/parity/escalations.md`; the human COBOL review the request names is tracked in `docs/parity/signoff.md`.

## Gates

A file gated by a section is written only when every row of that section has passed its review log.

| Section | Content | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| A. Record layouts | one row per elementary field of every record layout, FILLER included | crates/domain/src/numeric/**, crates/codec/src/layouts/**, migrations/0001 to 0004, crates/persistence/src/seed.rs |
| B. Per-program rules | paragraph decisions, key paths, file access, write persistence | crates/domain/src/rules/**, crates/domain/src/messages.rs, crates/domain/src/format.rs, crates/api/src/handlers/** (except rewards.rs and admin_reward_rules.rs), crates/batch/src/jobs/{posttran,intcalc,tranbkp,combtran,creastmt,tranrept,cbpaup0j,mnttrdb2}.rs, crates/messaging/src/flows/**, crates/messaging/src/error_queue.rs, every parity test |
| C. Arithmetic | receivers, truncation, worked values | as section B |
| D. Fixture expectations | results of the audited rules on the fixture corpus | as section B |
| E. Anomalies | defect-like paths and anomalous fixtures with their disposition | as section B |
| F. Time-dependent fields | formats of clock-dependent output | as section B |

## Conventions

- Tables are GitHub pipe tables, one record per line; a literal `|` inside a cell is written `\|`.
- Row IDs are `P-<KEY>-<nnn>`; `<KEY>` equals the row's Program cell, and numbering per key runs continuously through sections A to F.
- Row IDs are never reused or renumbered, because code, tests and the other audits cite them; a row added to a key after its first numbering takes the key's next free number, so within a section a key's numbers can exceed those of its rows in a later section.
- Citations are `[<path>:L<n>]`, `[<path>:L<n>-<m>]` or `[<path>]`, with repository-relative paths in their stored case and 1-based physical line numbers of the stored file (never the COBOL sequence numbers in columns 1-6 or 73-80). Every data row carries at least one `path:L<n>` citation (`[<path>:L<n>]` or `[<path>:L<n>-<m>]`); a bare `[<path>]` is supplementary only and never a row's sole citation. Every Paragraph cell carries at least one citation. IBM manuals are cited by title in plain text.
- Byte offsets are 0-based; lengths are in bytes.
- An exact text is a code span holding a double-quoted string, with `\"` and `\\` as escapes; `width=<n>` after it means the value is right-padded with spaces to n bytes. `{FIELD}` stands for the content of that COBOL field in a STRING-built text, `{UNDEF:n}` for n bytes the COBOL never sets.
- Structured results are `key=value; key=value`, values being bare tokens or exact texts.
- Escalation IDs: E-01 to E-22 are the seeded log of `docs/parity/escalations.md`; the IDs listed in the last section of this file are raised here; any other cited ID is raised by `docs/parity/validation-audit.md` (E-44 to E-55 and E-73) or `docs/parity/function-map.md` (E-56 to E-64); every cited ID is defined in `docs/parity/escalations.md`.
- Persists on later failure: `persists: RECOVERY(NONE)` for VSAM writes [app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:L1-96], or the commit or rollback the program issues for Db2 and IMS writes; `n/a` where a path has at most one write.

## A. Record layouts

Codec facts confirmed against the bytes: every signed DISPLAY field in the nine ASCII fixture files uses a trailing overpunch (`{ABCDEFGHI` for +0 to +9, `}JKLMNOPQR` for -0 to -9); the twelve codec layouts (the nine fixture copybooks, CSUSR01Y, the reject record and CVTRA05Y as the transaction output) have no COMP, COMP-3, REDEFINES or OCCURS; the FILLER of DISCGRP, TCATBAL, TRANTYPE and TRANCATG holds the character 0. No contrary byte was found.

| P-COACTUPC-041 | COACTUPC | 3310-PROTECT-ALL-ATTRS, 3320-UNPROTECT-FEW-ATTRS [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3441-3495] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3500-3561] | the attribute bytes (suffix A) of CACTUPAI; DFHBMPRF, DFHBMFSE (DFHBMSCA) | 3310 on every 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS; 3320 in states S and E | attributes=3310: DFHBMPRF on ACCTSID, status, the five money fields, open, expiry and reissue year, month and day, group ID, customer ID, SSN parts, FICO, DOB parts, names, address lines 1-2, city, state, zip, country, phone parts, government ID, EFT account, primary holder and INFOMSG; 3320: DFHBMFSE on status, the five money fields, the three dates, DOB, group ID, SSN parts, FICO, names, address lines 1-2, city, state, zip, phone parts, government ID, EFT account and primary holder, and DFHBMPRF again on ACSTNUM [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3531], ACSCTRY [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3547] and INFOMSG [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3560], while ACCTSID keeps the 3310 DFHBMPRF; DFHBMPRF is protected with the MDT on and DFHBMFSE unprotected with the MDT on (IBM CICS Transaction Server, BMS attribute constants DFHBMSCA), so RECEIVE MAP returns the displayed customer ID and country and COACTUPC never receives other values for them (E-74); group ID, address line 2 and government ID are editable and have no 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS edit | n/a |
| P-COACTUPC-042 | COACTUPC | 3390-SETUP-INFOMSG-ATTRS [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3566-3583] [app/bms/COACTUP.bms:L498-507] | INFOMSGA, FKEY05A, FKEY12A of CACTUPAI; WS-INFO-MSG X(40) | every 3000-SEND-MAP, after 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS | attributes=INFOMSG: WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE -> DFHBMDAR (dark), else DFHBMASB (bright); the dark branch never runs, because 3250 [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L2955-2977] always leaves a non-blank WS-INFO-MSG; F12=Cancel bright (DFHBMASB) when ACUP-CHANGES-MADE and not ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE (states E, N, L, F); PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION (state N) -> F5=Save and F12=Cancel bright; otherwise both stay ASKIP,DRK as COACTUP.bms defines them; replacement: the Save and Cancel controls (F-COACTUP-005, F-COACTUP-006), presentation free | n/a |
| P-COACTUPC-043 | COACTUPC | 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3650-3697] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L581-582] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3620-3622] | CARD-XREF-RECORD (CVACT03Y) RIDFLD WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X X(11); ERROR-RESP, ERROR-RESP2 X(10) | 9000-READ-ACCT with a valid key (ENTER on the key screen, or PF12) | access=EXEC CICS READ DATASET('CXACAIX ') RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) KEYLENGTH 11 INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD); NORMAL -> CDEMO-CUST-ID=XREF-CUST-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM=XREF-CARD-NUM; NOTFND -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, error=`"Account:"`+{WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X}+`" not found in"`+`" Cross ref file.  Resp:"`+{ERROR-RESP}+`" Reas:"`+{ERROR-RESP2} DELIMITED BY SIZE, only when no earlier message (V-COACTUPC-004, kind=NotFound, E-44); OTHER -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, ERROR-OPNAME='READ', ERROR-FILE='CXACAIX ', WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE moved to WS-RETURN-MSG without the message guard (V-COACTUPC-005, kind=Unexpected); 9000-READ-ACCT stops after either failure | n/a |
| P-COACTUPC-044 | COACTUPC | 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3701-3747] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3627-3629] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L499-500] | ACCOUNT-RECORD (CVACT01Y) RIDFLD WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X X(11) | cross-reference read NORMAL | access=EXEC CICS READ DATASET('ACCTDAT ') by the 11-byte account key INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD); NORMAL -> FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER; NOTFND -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, error=`"Account:"`+{WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X}+`" not found in"`+`" Acct Master file.Resp:"`+{ERROR-RESP}+`" Reas:"`+{ERROR-RESP2} only when no earlier message (V-COACTUPC-006, kind=NotFound, E-44); OTHER -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, File Error with ERROR-FILE='ACCTDAT ' without the guard (V-COACTUPC-007, kind=Unexpected); 9000-READ-ACCT then tests DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT, an 88 of WS-RETURN-MSG whose text 9300 never sets (its SET is commented out [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3719]), so the customer read still runs (E-45); when the customer is found, 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA stores the details, the account ones from the ACCOUNT-RECORD the failed READ did not fill, storage without VALUE that nothing in the task sets [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L640], so the account bytes stored and then shown by 3202 are unpinned (E-25), and 2000-DECIDE-ACTION sets state S [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L2577-2579] with the not-found text kept | n/a |
| P-COACTUPC-045 | COACTUPC | 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3752-3796] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3631] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3636-3643] [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L501-502] | CUSTOMER-RECORD (CVCUS01Y) RIDFLD WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X X(9) | after 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT, whatever its outcome | access=EXEC CICS READ DATASET('CUSTDAT ') by CDEMO-CUST-ID, the cross-reference customer ID (9 bytes), INTO(CUSTOMER-RECORD); NORMAL -> FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER; NOTFND -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK, error=`"CustId:"`+{WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X}+`" not found"`+`" in customer master.Resp: "`+{ERROR-RESP}+`" REAS:"`+{ERROR-RESP2} only when no earlier message (V-COACTUPC-008, kind=NotFound, E-44); OTHER -> INPUT-ERROR, FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK, File Error with ERROR-FILE='CUSTDAT ' without the guard, overwriting an earlier text (V-COACTUPC-009, kind=Unexpected); the DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT test never matches (its SET is commented out [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L3769]), so 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA still runs and stores customer fields from the CUSTOMER-RECORD the failed READ did not fill, storage without VALUE [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L646] (E-25); on the key-screen path FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER then stays off and 2000-DECIDE-ACTION leaves the details not fetched [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L2577-2579], so 3201 shows none of them; on the PF12 re-read 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS has already set FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER [app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl:L1456], so state S follows even when a read fails, and after a failed customer read 3202 shows those unpinned bytes | n/a |

## D. Fixture expectations

### D.1 POSTTRAN reject set

Keys: record_no, tran_id, reason, description, bytes, card, account_id, ws_temp_bal, acct_credit_limit, acct_expiraion_date, orig_date, read, posted, rejected, exit

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. POSTTRAN runs CBTRN02C over all 300 records of dailytran.txt with the clock pinned to 2022-07-01T12:00:00Z; validation order 100, 101, 102, 103 (103 overwrites 102); accepted records update the cycle totals before the next record is checked. Every reject of the corpus is reason 0102: the 103 test passes for all of them. Used by crates/batch/tests/posttran_rejects.rs.

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. Values are the account and category balance records after POSTTRAN (D.1 run). Category keys absent from tcatbal.txt are created by 2700-A from the first posted record with that key.

### D.3 INTCALC

Keys: account_id, tran_type_cd, tran_cat_cd, group, rate, tran_cat_bal, monthly_interest, tran_id, total_interest, updated, acct_curr_bal, acct_curr_cyc_credit, acct_curr_cyc_debit, systran_tran_id, card_number, kind, records, first, last

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. INTCALC runs CBACT04C with --parm-date 2022071800 [app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:L22] over the category balances after POSTTRAN (D.2), in key order. Every ACCT-GROUP-ID is blank (E-06), so every rate comes from the DEFAULT group.

### D.4 COMBTRAN

Keys: records, order, first, last, equal_keys, loaded, rejected, stopped_at, not_attempted, exit, live_master

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after POSTTRAN (D.1), INTCALC (D.3) and TRANBKP; the combined file is backup(0) followed by SYSTRAN(0), sorted by TRAN-ID. Interleaved rows apply the REPRO duplicate-key rows of section B (COMBTRAN STEP10) to the combined record numbers given; the corpus itself never reaches that case, because CT02 and CB00 cannot add to an empty live master (E-27).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| P-COMBTRAN-005 | COMBTRAN | STEP10 [app/jcl/COMBTRAN.jcl:L41-48] | TRANVSAM (live master) | README case: live master empty after TRANBKP | loaded=312; rejected=0; exit=0; live_master=the combined file, record for record |

### D.5 CREASTMT

Keys: cards, max_transactions_per_card, transactions, within_capacity, file, name, records, width, terminator, card_order, per_card_records, kind, line_no, text, card_number, account_id, customer_id, n

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after POSTTRAN, INTCALC, TRANBKP and COMBTRAN [README.md:L224-228]. A card statement has n transaction lines, n being its kind=card_summary row. Template rows hold for every card: in line_no, n is that count and i runs from 1 to n. Variable rows give the absolute line number within the card. Cards follow in card-number order. {UNDEF:k} stands for k bytes the COBOL never sets (E-25): the replacement writes spaces there, which also keeps the HTML STRING DELIMITED BY '*' from stopping early.

### D.6 TRANREPT

Keys: records_in_range, lines, width, terminator, order, line_no, kind, text, tran_id, total

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. State after batch seed and batch posttran with CARDDEMO_CLOCK_OVERRIDE=2022-07-01T12:00:00Z, so every posted record carries PROC-TS 2022-07-01 and falls inside 2022-01-01..2022-07-06; tranrept backs up the live master, keeps the in-range records, sorts them by card number and runs CBTRN03C.

### D.7 Seed counts

Keys: table, rows, tran_cat_bal

Derivation: a throwaway script outside the repository applies the cited section B and C rows to the fixture records in file order, starting from the seeded state (every fixture file loaded by batch seed, TRANSACT empty, IMS and Db2 authorization stores empty) and decoding every field by its section A offsets. Counts are the records of each fixture file, the Db2 initial load rows and the DUSRSECJ SYSUT1 rows. Used by crates/persistence/tests/seed.rs.

### D.10 CP00 examples
